title: Underestimation
text: “Oink…”
“Huh? Elena’s staying behind in the carriage? Again?”

When the carriage stopped near the building housing the Dragon Hourglass, the Lazy Pig grunted that to my Father. Just how much of a pain in the neck is this guy? I, Motoyasu, find myself thinking about killing the Lazy Pig at every opportunity. …But if I actually did it, my Father would get mad at me, so I’ll hold back.

Incidentally, since the Lazy Pig is the child of nobility, she’s reportedly waiting in the carriage because showing up at an important facility like the Dragon Hourglass might draw the attention of the Three Heroes Church or other nobles. Pigs really do use their wits—but only when it comes to their own interests.
“Well… it’s not such a big errand, so I’ll be back pretty soon… Alright then, Elena, you stay here and watch the place.”
“Oink…”
“Sakura’s coming.”
“Kou too—”
“It’s practically no different from what we saw in Siltvelt.”
“Is that so? Then Kou’ll wait here.”
“I’m going.”
It seems Yuki-chan is coming along as well. Since Sakura-chan considers protecting her Father her mission, she appears to be accompanying Keel. She’s holding Keel, who’s in his puppy form.
“Let’s go!”

Barking and wagging his tail, Keel is being carried cheerfully by Sakura-chan as he holds out his paws. Father is watching the scene with a look that seems to say it’s heartwarming. Their destination is the Dragon Hourglass!
“Oink.”

As they entered the building housing the Dragon Hourglass, a pig came out to greet them. Its attitude… isn’t exactly friendly. I almost instinctively aimed my spear at it. When the time comes, I’ll turn this guy into a pile of charcoal too.
“Ah, I heard there’d be waves tomorrow, so I came.”

My Father replied with a somewhat displeased expression. Guided by the pig, we made our way right up to the Dragon Hourglass. …Since my Father has already seen the Dragon Hourglass in Siltvelt, he doesn’t seem to have any particular thoughts on it.

Oh, right—the sand from the Dragon Hourglass, which is the material for the weapon that grants the Portal skill in the first world, was actually what we received that very day. After my Father left with Big Sister looking rather displeased, the Pig brought it over. Of course, I had also asked him for it as a material.

Judging by my conversation with my Father afterward, he definitely hadn’t received the sand from the Hourglass. He didn’t seem to know about it until I mentioned it, so I’m sure of it. ……This is a trick, you know.
“Father, could you lend me a ear for a moment?”
“Hm? What is it, Motoyasu?”
I whispered what had just occurred to me to my Father.
“Huh? Oh… I see.”
Nodding, my Father stood right in front of the Dragon Hourglass. Then, a beam of light shot from the Hourglass toward his shield, telling us the arrival time of the wave.
“Yeah. So the wave really is coming tomorrow, huh?”

After confirming the wave’s arrival time, my Father nodded repeatedly. Since this is the first wave we’ll be fighting, it shouldn’t be too much of a struggle. Once we get past tomorrow’s wave, we’ll be able to focus on peddling again, so I’d like to get this over with quickly.
“That’s right. This will be your first wave, Father, but I hope you’ll face it without fear.”
“It’s okay—I think I’ve made as much preparation as I possibly could…”
“Sakura will do her best, too!”
“Me too, me too!”
Just as we were talking like that, as expected, Itsuki called out to us from behind.
“Oh? Isn’t that Motoyasu-san and Naofumi…-san over there?”

Come to think of it, I’d been looking around inside the building where the Dragon Hourglass is, but when I ran into my Father, Itsuki and Ren had just arrived. After all, if Ren and Itsuki weren’t coming, there’d be no reason for me to be here right now.

I turned around and looked toward Itsuki. Hmm? That guy who looks like a Crimson Swine isn’t here? Where could he be? I was hoping to keep an eye on his movements too… Just as I was looking around around Itsuki, Ren and his crew showed up.
“What’s up with you guys? Is there some kind of gathering going on?”
“Nah, nothing in particular…”
“We haven’t seen each other since then… but it looks like Naofumi’s made some friends of his own.”

Ren said in a matter-of-fact tone. It seemed Ren was somewhat concerned about my Father. After all, he’d lost trust in the Crimson Swine and the Trash King because of their outrageous actions. You could say that was a natural reaction.
“W-well, yeah.”
“You’re being evasive. Don’t you have some idea what’s going on?”

My father glared at Itsuki with a scowling expression. It was as if he were saying, “I don’t have to answer to you.” And rightly so! He doesn’t have the slightest right to say that to Itsuki. That Messiah complex of his!

To see a pig’s tears and have no room for doubt—that’s the sort of thing a fool would do. That’s right! Just like I used to be! Pigs are depraved lifeforms capable of shedding false tears for their own gain at any moment. All pigs are beings that should be exterminated. When the time comes this time around, I’ll reduce the Crimson Swine to a pile of ashes.
Silence reigned over the room. Is Father saying the atmosphere is awkward? Even if we were to talk, there doesn’t seem to be much to discuss.
Come to think of it, in the first world, after Father stormed out looking displeased, we went ahead and did the Class Up for Ryo and Itsuki’s companions, didn’t we? Well then, I’ll take the lead.
“Have Ren and Itsuki come to Class Up their party members?”
“Well… yes.”
“What about you two?”
“Um…”

My father seems at a loss for words. We’ve already Classed Up, but since we didn’t do it in Melromarc, saying we’ve already done it would render all our actions up to this point meaningless. So, it’s safest to just say that Classing Up is still a ways off.

I sense that the pig in charge of the church is grinning at us. He’s probably thinking something like, “You don’t even have high enough levels to be talking about Class Up.” Father is particularly sensitive to any hint of being mocked, so I, Motoyasu, am doing my best to stifle my laughter.
This is precisely part of the plan that Father has been executing up until today. If the enemy underestimates us, it makes the battle that much easier. It seems the plan is working just as intended.
“I was just trying to figure out how long until the next wave.”
“Well, that’s fine, isn’t it? Since you’re weak, don’t go doing anything reckless during the wave.”
“…Y-yeah, you’re right.”
You can tell Father is feeling annoyed by Ren’s condescending tone. However, he bit his tongue and replied with a smile.
“All right, all right. Well then, maybe I’ll just watch you guys go through Class Up?”
“Well, with gear like that, Class Up still seems a long way off.”
“I suppose so.”

For a moment, Father’s eyebrows twitched, but he put on a smirk of contempt. Well, the gear here in Siltvelt is several tiers above what Ren and Itsuki are wearing. Ren, Itsuki—you two had better bask in your sense of superiority while you still can.
“What did you say! Big bro, you see—”
Enraged by Ren and Itsuki’s remarks, Keel tried to lunge forward, but Father held him back from behind.
“It’ll be fine… okay? Sakura-chan, try to keep your anger in check, too.”

My father cautioned Sakura-chan as she reached for the hilts of the two swords strapped to her waist. If she didn’t, both of them would end up dead. In their current state, Ren and Itsuki wouldn’t stand a chance against either Keel or Sakura-chan.
…After all, they are supposed to be heroes. Surely they aren’t that weak, are they? Well, in my estimation, they’re about on par in terms of combat strength.
“Still… you’ve got some unusual companions with you.”

Ren says this as he looks at my Father and me. What does Filolial-sama mean by “unusual companions”? Filolial-sama and his kind are the ultimate and supreme beings. “Don’t lump me in with a loner like you!” is what he’s saying.
“A Demi-Human with wings on its back…?”

Ren stares intently at Sakura-chan and Yuki-chan. That’s completely wrong. He’s got eyes like a blind man. To mistake the noble form of Filolial-sama for a Demi-Human… Ren’s knowledge of games is clearly limited. Well, my own knowledge of games was pretty much the same trash, though.
